name: Ronald Reagan
role: 40th President of the United States (1981-1989); Governor of California (1967-1975)
summary: A conservative Republican who cut top income tax rates, deregulated industry and sought to shrink domestic spending, while building up the military against the Soviet Union. He opposed abortion, favored states' rights and school prayer, and signed both tougher drug laws and a broad immigration amnesty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Said in 1983 that the $3.35 minimum wage should not apply to young people.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: 'A government can't control the economy without controlling people'; 'the more the plans fail, the more the planners plan.'

public-ownership.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cut the top income tax rate from 70% to 50% in 1981 and to 28% in 1986, criticizing 'a tax system which penalizes successful achievement.'

unions-good.rationale: Fired more than 10,000 striking PATCO air traffic controllers in 1981.

property-fundamental.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

regulate-corporations.rationale: About half of federal regulations in place in 1981 were eliminated by 1986; deregulated savings and loans and cut the EPA's budget.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said welfare rolls grow rather than shrink ('the need grows greater; the program grows greater') and cut food stamps, school lunches and Medicaid in 1981; called the welfare system 'misguided' (1986).

worker-ownership.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: 'Drugs are menacing our society' (1986); signed the Anti-Drug Abuse Acts of 1986 and 1988 with mandatory minimum penalties.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

strong-leader.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

state-harmful.rationale: 'Government is not the solution to our problem; government is the problem' (1981), while leading the government and expanding the military.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed California's Mulford Act (1967) and a 1986 ban on civilian sales of new fully automatic weapons, later endorsed the Brady bill and the 1994 assault-weapons ban, while also signing the Firearm Owners Protection Act.

empower-police-military.rationale: Led a major military buildup and pledged to 'maintain sufficient strength to prevail if need be'; expanded drug enforcement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

decide-locally.rationale: 'The Federal Government did not create the States; the States created the Federal Government' (1981); argued civil rights laws infringed on states' rights (1988).

rehabilitation.rationale: Supported capital punishment and refused clemency to Aaron Mitchell as governor; signed mandatory minimum drug sentences.

traditional-family.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Opposed the 1978 Briggs Initiative against gay teachers, but said in 1984 'We will resist the efforts of some to obtain government endorsement of homosexuality.'

abortion-legal.rationale: Regretted signing California's 1967 abortion law, said 'unless and until someone can prove the unborn human is not alive' it should be protected (1982), and backed barring federal abortion funding.

more-religion-public.rationale: Proposed a constitutional amendment in 1982 to allow voluntary school prayer, saying 'the first amendment is being turned on its head.'

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Opposed the 1964 Civil Rights Act on property-rights grounds and vetoed the 1988 Civil Rights Restoration Act, though he signed a 25-year Voting Rights Act extension in 1982.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

gradual-change.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Signed the 1986 Immigration Reform and Control Act, which legalized about three million undocumented immigrants so they could 'step into the sunlight,' while banning the knowing hiring of undocumented workers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposed 'subordinating American interests to an organization that has become so structurally unsound' as the UN (1964).

free-trade.rationale: Proposed a 'North American accord' in 1979 that became NAFTA, though he imposed a temporary 100% tariff on some Japanese electronics.

nation-first.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported anti-communist forces such as the Nicaraguan Contras, invaded Grenada (1983) and bombed Libya (1986).

limit-growth.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Lamented air pollution regulations (1980), pledged to abolish the Department of Energy and dismissed acid rain proposals as burdensome to industry.
